UPSTREAM: google/chromeos: Add recovery module in vboot2 Add recovery module in vboot2 that checks if a recovery request is pending and returns appropriate reason code: 1. Checks if recovery mode is initiated by EC. 2. Checks if recovery request is present in VBNV. 3. Checks if recovery request is present in handoff for post-cbmem stages. 4. Checks if vboot verification is complete and looks up selected region to identify if recovery is requested by vboot library. UPSTREAM: google/chromeos: Add support for saving recovery reason across reboot On some x86 platforms (skylake, apollolake), we observe reboots at different steps during the FSP initialization. These additional reboots result in loss of recovery request because vboot_reference library clears recovery request on vbnv once verification is complete and it has made a decision about which boot path to take(normal/dev, slot-a/slot-b, recovery). Provide a way to allow mainboards/chipsets to inform recovery module in vboot2 to save recovery reason to survive unexpected reboots. The recovery reason is set in vbnv after vboot_reference library completes its verification and clears the reason in vbnv while jumping to payload. BUG=chrome-os-partner:55431 BRANCH=None TEST=None Signed-off-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/15802 Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org> Change-Id: Ie96be9aeb42c8209d8215943409e6327d6a8bf98 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/362974 Commit-Ready: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org>

Fix yaml pkg-config warnings I see warnings like this when building with USE=minimal (the default): Package yaml-0.1 was not found in the pkg-config search path. Perhaps you should add the directory containing `yaml-0.1.pc' to the PKG_CONFIG_PATH environment variable No package 'yaml-0.1' found That's because we don't have a yaml dependency for the USE=minimal build, yet we still unconditionally call `pkg-config --libs yaml-0.1`. Let's move the pkg-config calls into 'ifeq' block where they're actually used. BRANCH=none BUG=none TEST=`emerge-${BOARD} vboot_reference` both with and without USE=minimal Change-Id: I96a59848ee970abacbe4cc3c56bb35c7cf552f63 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/362620 Reviewed-by: Randall Spangler <rspangler@chromium.org>

login: Record cumulative arc uptime metric Intruduces a class for tracking cumulative usage time (started and stopped when ARC container is started and stopped). The class (CumulativeUseTimeMetric) tracks usage time by increasing value of tracked usage time in regular intervals (5 min), occasionally sending the aggregated value to UMA. The value is sent to UMA at most once a day. The tracked value is persisted to file system in order to avoid losing accumulated values when device reboots, especially on dirty shutdown (there still may be loss in this case, but it's amount of time since last update instead of amount of time since tracking is started). When sending data to UMA, only time accumulated for current OS version is included - when initializing usage tracking on OS version update, any data collected for previous OS version is disregarded. BUG=b:28815532 TEST=manual/unittests Change-Id: Ia785d8c48ef739e41fdbc49edbe6ef094dfe530c Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/361042 Commit-Ready: Toni Barzic <tbarzic@chromium.org> Tested-by: Toni Barzic <tbarzic@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>
